title: Rafael and the Atlas
premise: In the waning years of the Republic of Vessany, Isandro Hartwell carries a diplomatic cipher sealed to her skin, posing as a widowed mapmaker's daughter in a border town where everyone has learned to forget on command. When a census taker named Rafael begins asking questions no census requires, Isandro realizes her family of strays—the deaf archivist Ovid, the runaway heir Sef, and old Marta who remembers too much—has been flagged for extraction lists that decide who survives the coming annexation. As the cipher she carries turns out to name the very people worth saving, Isandro must decode it, betray the mission she was sworn to complete, and choose which of them takes the last berth on the evacuation ship before the century turns. She gives the berth to Sef, stays behind with Rafael, and discovers that inheritance is not what we keep but what we hand to someone still moving.
about_author: Zephyrine Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records from collapsed states. They write historical fiction about the paperwork of survival and live between two coastlines with an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: The Question That Wasn't on the Form
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During the annual census, Rafael lingers over her household entry and asks whether anyone in the house has ever held a commission. Isandro lies smoothly, but that night she checks the cipher against her ribs and finds the seal has begun to itch—a sensation she'd been told was impossible. Beat: dread arriving politely.

chapters.title: A Household of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet the family: Ovid cataloguing banned hymnals by feel, Sef forging shipping manifests, Marta burning letters she claims not to read. Isandro inventories their small economies of silence. The chapter establishes what she stands to lose. Beat: tenderness sharpened into vigilance.

chapters.title: What the Courier Swallowed
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Isandro's POV. Fifteen years earlier, she took the courier's oath and the cipher implantation in a hospital corridor that smelled of vinegar. Her handler told her the code would name itself when the republic needed it. It never did. Beat: the origin of her expertise in silence.

chapters.title: Rafael Returns Without a Census Book
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He comes back ostensibly to correct an ink error, actually to watch Isandro's hands while she pours tea. He knows couriers' hands. He was a courier once, for the other side now winning. Beat: two professionals recognizing each other across a table neither trusts.

chapters.title: Ovid Reads the Room
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV, rendered through his deafness—vibration, breath, the grammar of doors. He notices Rafael's second visit and tells Isandro in their private sign-language that the man walks like someone counting exits. First family council: do they run? Beat: fear becoming strategy.

chapters.title: The Extraction Lists
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef, forging manifests at the harbor office, copies a document he shouldn't see: a priority list of persons for 'resettlement,' with three names from their street—and a blank line where a fourth should be. Beat: the machinery of survival revealed as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Marta's Century
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Born in the republic's first year, she remembers its founding promises and its first betrayal. She recognizes the list format from a purge forty years ago and teaches Isandro how families used to trade places on it. Beat: inheritance as dangerous instruction.

chapters.title: The Cipher Speaks
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Under stress, the seal finally releases: the cipher isn't a treaty text—it's a roster of protected individuals, and the final entry is blank, assignable by the carrier alone. One guaranteed berth on the last ship out. Beat: revelation as burden; the mission was always a choice.

chapters.title: Everyone Learns the Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She tells the family there is one berth. No one argues; that's the horror. Ovid offers himself first, then withdraws it so no one can accept. Sef gets angry at being considered at all. Marta says the quiet thing: 'Decide before you love us more.' Beat: love under audit.

chapters.title: Rafael's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. We see his own cost: he survived his republic's fall by carrying names, and half of them died anyway. His superiors want Isandro's cipher recovered intact; the person inside it is irrelevant. He begins falsifying his reports—one day's delay at a time. Beat: complicity turning toward mercy.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef scouts the evacuation berth and meets the harbormaster's daughter, Ilse, who is running her own smaller rescue of forged papers. A fragile alliance forms. Beat: hope that feels like contraband.

chapters.title: What Ovid Kept
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV. He reveals he has spent years transcribing the town's forbidden histories into braille boards hidden in the archive wall—an inheritance meant for whoever remains. He asks Isandro to promise the record will outlive any of them. Beat: legacy larger than one life.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Small Things
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. His superior arrives early, suspicious of the delayed reports, and interviews the household separately. Marta performs senility brilliantly; Sef nearly breaks; Isandro watches Rafael decide, question by question, which side of the form he's on. Beat: the climax's fuse lit.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Vinegar
chapters.summary: Isandro and Rafael, shared POV alternating scenes. In the old courier hospital, Rafael offers a trade: he'll certify the roster as corrupted if Isandro surrenders the physical seal—but only one name can ride the exemption. The arithmetic shrinks to its cruelest size. Beat: negotiation as intimacy.

chapters.title: The Night of Three Goodbyes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Each family member privately tries to give Isandro the berth: Ovid signs it into her palm, Marta leaves her wedding ring as payment for passage, Sef simply packs her bag. Isandro understands they've all decided she's the one who should live. Beat: grief rehearsed in advance.

chapters.title: Annexation Day
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The republic formally dissolves; troops arrive with the new flag and new forms. The harbor closes at dusk. The ship's manifest must be final by noon. Everything converges on a single gangplank and a single name-line. Beat: history as deadline.

chapters.title: The Berth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, climax part one. At the gangplank, Isandro writes Sef's name into the blank line—he is the youngest, the heir to nothing, the one with the most future to inherit. Sef refuses; Ovid physically lifts him onto the deck. The ship sounds its horn. Beat: the choice made with hands, not words.

chapters.title: What Rafael Did With the Seal
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, climax part two. Rafael submits the corrupted roster, burning his own career to make the exemption untraceable. His superior arrests him for negligence rather than treason—a sentence designed to forget him. Beat: sacrifice rendered as paperwork.

chapters.title: The Archive Wall
chapters.summary: Isandro, Ovid, and Marta's POV. Under occupation, the remaining family seals Ovid's braille histories into the wall and scatters duplicates through Ilse's paper network. The town goes back to forgetting—but now forgetting has a backup. Beat: resistance as memory-keeping.

chapters.title: Letters That Take Two Years
chapters.summary: Epistolary chapter. Sef's letters arrive from across the sea via Ilse's network: clumsy, funny, alive. He has found the republic's exiled archivists and given them Ovid's first duplicate. Isandro reads aloud to the house. Beat: distance measured in gratitude.

chapters.title: The New Census
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A year later, a new empire's census taker knocks. Isandro answers every question truthfully—her real name among them—for the first time in fifteen years. Rafael, released and unrecognizable in civilian clothes, waits in her kitchen. Beat: visibility chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: Atlas
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, coda. She finishes the mapbook she began as cover identity and sends it to Sef: a hand-drawn atlas of everywhere their family ever hid, each hiding place marked with who waited there. Inheritance, she writes, is the route, not the treasure. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
